items.title: Religious affairs dept urges ‘solat hajat’, aid for residents after Serian haze emergency
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 5 — The Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) has called on mosques and surau in the Federal Territories to hold solat hajat (special prayers), seeking relief from the haze and protection for residents affected by worsening air pollution in Serian, Sarawak. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the department respected His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia’s consent to declare a haze emergency in the Serian Division following air pollution levels that posed a threat to public health and safety. Earlier, Sultan Ibrahim consented to the declaration of a haze emergency throughout the Serian Division after air pollution levels reached a stage deemed hazardous to public health and safety.

items.title: Smart team deployed to Nepal for humanitarian mission
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: An 11-man team from Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) departed today to take part in a humanitarian mission in Nepal. The rescue team left Subang Air Base aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) A400M aircraft at about 9am, carrying various equipment, including communications gear. The mission is led by Smart commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa, with the flight expected to take about five hours.

items.title: German President calls for unity in democracy ahead of landmark vote
items.summary: BONN, (Germany): German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier on Friday called for the country's democracy and rule of law be protected from those "who scorn and trample all over them," ahead of Sunday's state election that can bring the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) to power. "Ethnic-based thinking and nationalist isolationism are simply not the answer to the challenges of the 21st century," Steinmeier told a community festival attended by 2,000 volunteers at his secondary residence in Bonn, reported German news agency dpa. It helps to realise that those who wish to protect and preserve democracy represent the majority, said Steinmeier.

items.title: DOE raises monitoring and enforcement to highest level after Serian haze emergency declared
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Department of Environment (DOE) will raise air quality monitoring and preparedness to the highest level following the declaration of a haze emergency in the Serian Division, Sarawak, after the Air Pollutant Index (API) reached a hazardous level of 477 last night. DOE Deputy Director-General (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the department would strengthen monitoring and field operations in line with the National Haze Action Plan (NHAP) and NADMA Directive No. 1: National Disaster Management Policy and Mechanism.

items.title: #NSTviral: Pagoh bus rescue highlights Malaysian spirit [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing Malaysians helping passengers escape an overturned express bus in Johor has won praise on social media, with many hailing it as a display of unity. The footage showed passengers helping one another evacuate after the bus' main door became inaccessible. "This is the Malaysia that we all love and want – one heart, one soul, helping one another and sharing every burden," Threads user @alyarazaliii wrote.

items.title: Anwar visits Egyptian scholar Sheikh Abdul Aziz, who urges preservation of Islamic classical heritage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Prominent Egyptian scholar Sheikh Abdul Aziz al-Syahawi has advised that Islamic classical heritage ( turath ) must continue to be preserved, while new technology should be leveraged to document and sustain Islamic scholarly heritage. This message was delivered when Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim visited him at Nasyrul Quran, Putrajaya, this afternoon. Anwar stated in a social media post that Sheikh Abdul Aziz reminded that the preservation of turath is a responsibility because these treasures serve as a bridge connecting today’s generation to a long scholarly tradition.

items.title: Serian records 376 API reading as of 8am
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Serian in Sarawak recorded a hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 376 as of 8am today. Three other areas in the state, namely Kuching, Samarahan and Sri Aman recorded very unhealthy API readings at 273, 267 and 259 respectively. Other stations recording unhealthy readings were Labuan (161), Batu Pahat (156), Kluang and Larkin (155), Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (155), Johan Setia (154), Bukit Rambai, Segamat and Pasir Gudang (153), Tangkak (152), Kota Tinggi (151), Kimanis (145), Romping (139), Balok Baru (118) and Kota Kinabalu (113) A total of 30 stations recorded moderate API readings, while 10 recorded good readings.

items.title: US midterms begin with chaos over mail-voting crackdown
items.summary: WASHINGTON: America's midterm elections opened Friday in a fog of confusion over mail voting, with ballots already going out as President Donald Trump presses courts to let him impose sweeping new restrictions on how they are handled. Yet voters and election officials still do not know what rules may govern millions of mail ballots, as Trump asks the Supreme Court to revive curbs blocked by a federal judge and as states scramble to prepare for changes that could come after voting has begun. Rules in limbo Trump's March executive order would require states to provide the US Postal Service with lists of eligible mail voters through a new federal portal.

items.title: Malaysians grateful for help at critical moment
items.summary: Tarmimi said the uncertainty over whether airports would remain open and routes would remain safe was more exhausting than the physical journey itself. Relief came when they reached Jeddah Airport, where Malaysian authorities had arranged an evacuation flight home. For Malaysian student Hanees Shafe, an umrah similarly turned into anxious uncertainty when conflict erupted in the Middle East and the Malaysian Embassy in Saudi Arabia offered her a flight home.

items.title: Freedom Flotilla announces new mission to Gaza in October
items.summary: ISTANBUL: The Freedom Flotilla Coalition announced a new international maritime mission to the Gaza Strip, with vessels making stops at European ports before a planned attempt to reach the enclave in October, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported. The mission seeks to challenge Israel's blockade of Gaza and mobilise public pressure across Europe, the coalition said in a statement published Wednesday. The mission brings together human rights advocates, trade union activists, elected representatives, journalists, medical professionals and other supporters of Palestinian rights, the coalition said.

items.title: Mexican ruling-party lawmaker found dead with gunshot wound, a year before elections
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: A member of Congress from Mexico's ruling Morena party was found dead from a gunshot wound in the eastern state of Veracruz on Friday, less than a year before local and federal elections. Zenyazen Escobar, a federal legislator representing the coastal state — home to some of the country's oil complexes — was found dead inside his car with at least one gunshot wound. "The investigation file is being compiled," state Attorney General Lisbeth Jimenez told reporters, without providing further details.

items.title: Tetris distances itself from controversial White House 'arcade' games
items.summary: SAN FRANCISCO: Tetris said on Friday that it did not give permission for the White House to use the game's iconic imagery for a controversial online arcade that the Trump administration released on Thursday. The arcade-style games and promotional content used by the Trump administration contain images that resemble games created by Tetris and other major game developers, including Sega, Microsoft-owned Xbox and the Flappy Bird Foundation. The White House released several games Thursday, with a placeholder that teased another one "coming soon".

items.title: The new arms race is moving into space
items.summary: Both programmes reflect the rapidly evolving field of military space operations as Beijing and Washington prepare for the possibility of conflict extending into space. And the US and Britain conducted their first joint military operation in space in the path of a suspected Chinese spy satellite, according to commercial space-tracking data. "The Chinese are rapidly developing capabilities", including ground- and space-based weapons designed to interfere with or destroy targets, US Space Force's chief of space operations General Chance Saltzman said in July.

items.title: Panama Canal begins reducing crossings due to El Nino
items.summary: PANAMA CITY: The Panama Canal on Friday began reducing the number of ships passing through due to a drought caused by the El Nino weather phenomenon. The Panama Canal Authority said low water levels in the two artificial lakes that feed the canal forced it to act. In 2023, El Nino forced the canal authority to reduce the number of daily crossings to 22 vessels.

items.title: UN adopts new map with smaller US, bigger Africa
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: The United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe, drawing ire from Washington. The new map – known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection – improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world", the resolution said. It makes Africa, Latin America, South Asia and Oceania appear much larger.

items.title: UniMAP accelerates AI, semiconductor research
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Universiti Malaysia Perlis (UniMAP) is stepping up its artificial intelligence (AI) and semiconductor research drive to turn academic breakthroughs into practical solutions that strengthen Malaysia's industrial competitiveness. UniMAP vice-chancellor Datuk Professor Dr Zaliman Sauli said the university is committed to ensuring its research delivers tangible solutions to real-world challenges. Zaliman said GTEST 2026 reflected UniMAP's efforts to bridge the gap between research and impact.

items.title: Reclaiming our future from corruption
items.summary: LETTERS: I fully agree with the important message in Sharanjit Singh's NST article — it is truly time to put an end to corruption that takes so much from our country. The report shows that over 26 years, we have lost an estimated RM4.5 trillion. People from all levels — public officials, civil servants, and business leaders with titles — are being charged across both government and private sector establishments.

items.title: NST Leader: Gaza cannot be emptied in plain sight
items.summary: The Zionists began to move to Palestine in wave after wave beginning in 1882 when the modern Zionist colony was established in Rishon LeZion, falsely claiming that the land active with Arabs was "a land without people". Each wave was said to number 25,000 to 30,000 European Jews — not Palestinian Jews or Christians — escaping Russian persecution. The fact then and now is that Palestine was never a land without people nor was it meant for a people without land, a Zionist political slogan that took on a false religious narrative.

items.title: Najib, Rosmah legal wins, custody deaths and Shah Alam murder charges among key court cases this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: It was a week of significant legal victories for members of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's family, while the country's highest court paved the way for important questions on deaths in custody to be examined. Najib, his wife Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor and their son Datuk Mohd Nazifuddin each secured favourable rulings in separate proceedings. Meanwhile, the Federal Court agreed to hear appeals involving two deaths in custody, while eight men were charged with the murder of a 23-year-old man during a brawl in Shah Alam.

items.title: Trump says Iran war is 'small potatoes' for US
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said Friday that the Iran war was "small potatoes" for the US, in his administration's latest bid to play down the conflict ahead of crucial midterm elections. Trump's comments came a day after Vice President JD Vance said that "I wouldn't call it a war" despite an upsurge in clashes between Iran and the US over the Strait of Hormuz. I call it a military conflict because it's small potatoes for us," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office when asked about Vance's remarks.

items.title: Penang shooting, airport cannabis haul and RM260m oil seizure among key crime cases this week
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A manhunt is underway for two men who shot and injured a 43-year-old mechanic at a car workshop in Jalan Sungai Lembu, Bukit Mertajam, Penang on Aug 3. Police also found that the victim has a previous criminal record. The case is the second involving a Malaysian allegedly carrying hydroponic cannabis into Chennai within a month, after Indian Customs arrested a 54-year-old Malaysian from Perak with 4.033kg of the drug on Aug 8 after he arrived from Bangkok.

items.title: Beyond August 31 and September 16: National Archives urges deeper understanding of Malaysia’s nation‑building
items.summary: National Archives of Malaysia (ANM) director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor said public awareness of the country’s history is growing but there is still room to deepen understanding of the events and people behind these milestones. “Malaysians may know key dates such as August 31 and September 16, but understanding the processes, challenges, negotiations and contributions of the leaders who shaped independence and the formation of Malaysia is more important. ANM director-general Zaidin Mohd Noor speaks to Malay Mail during an interview.

items.title: Opponents seek to block US from starting work on Trump arch in Washington
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A group of three military veterans and an architectural historian on Friday asked a US judge to block the Trump administration from starting work on a triumphal arch in Washington. The US Interior Department on Thursday announced plans to move forward soon with work for the 250-foot (76-metre) arch near Arlington National Cemetery despite legal challenges and the lack of final approval from a government planning authority. In a US District Court filing on Friday seeking a temporary restraining order, lawyers for the plaintiffs said the administration has "no legal basis for the construction work".

items.title: US sinks third alleged Ecuador drug gang boat in a week
items.summary: QUITO: The US military said it had blown up another boat with alleged links to Ecuadoran drug gangs, bringing to three the number of vessels it has sunk in the area in a week. Thursday's operation by US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) is part of a broader US campaign of strikes on alleged Latin American drug boats that have left more than 200 people dead since last year. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM) said on X it struck a vessel "operating as a floating refuelling station in support of illicit at-sea drug trafficking operations" in the Eastern Pacific.

items.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill three
items.summary: BEIRUT: Israeli strikes in southern and eastern Lebanon late on Friday killed at least three people and injured 23, the Lebanese Health Ministry said. The ministry said in a statement that strikes hit five locations in the southern Tyr and Nabatieh regions and the Bekaa region in the east. The strikes came despite a truce between Israel and the Iran-backed Hizbollah fighter group.

items.title: Trump says envoys taking plan to 'end the war' to Moscow, Kyiv
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday that he was sending envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to end the four-year-old Ukraine war. It will be the first time that Trump's son-in-law Kushner and businessman friend Witkoff have visited war-torn Kyiv since Trump returned to office last year with a vow to solve the conflict. "I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators.

items.title: Massive fire breaks out at iconic Chew Jetty in Penang [WATCH]
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A massive fire broke out at Chew Jetty here this morning, with firefighters rushing to the scene to put out the blaze. Chew Jetty, one of George Town's best-known waterfront landmarks, is the largest and one of the oldest of Penang's Chinese clan jetties. The waterfront community remains known for its traditional stilt houses, wooden walkways and rich Chinese heritage.

items.title: Massive late-night crash completely blocks NKVE northbound [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All northbound lanes of the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) near Shah Alam were blocked following a late-night accident, bringing traffic to a standstill shortly before midnight. The accident occurred at Km8.4 on the northbound stretch from Setia Alam towards Shah Alam. In an update at 11.27pm, PLUS Malaysia Bhd (PLUS) said all northbound lanes were blocked and advised motorists to exit at the Setia Alam toll plaza and use alternative routes.

items.title: Serian haze emergency: DOE ramps up monitoring, enforcement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Environment (DOE) has raised air quality monitoring and preparedness to the highest level after a haze emergency was declared in Serian, Sarawak, where the Air Pollutant Index (API) hit 477 last night. DOE deputy director‑general (development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said monitoring and field operations will be strengthened under the National Haze Action Plan (NHAP) and Nadma Directive No. She stressed that DOE's jurisdiction covers environmental quality monitoring, prevention and enforcement against open burning and pollution sources under environmental laws.

items.title: 'Election stunt' jibes won't stop Ab Rauf from backing p-hailing riders
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh remains unfazed by claims that his recent ride-along with p-hailing workers was merely an "election stunt", saying his priority is to understand their challenges and find ways to help. He said joining a delivery rider's routine gave him a closer insight into the fatigue, road risks and responsibilities faced by p-hailing workers supporting their families. He said the state government's efforts to support p-hailing workers predated his ride-along last Wednesday, when he accepted and delivered a food order to experience their working conditions firsthand.

items.title: Judge declares mistrial in Lindsay Clancy child-killing case, puts ruling on hold for appeal
items.summary: Judge William Sullivan said he was freezing his mistrial ruling in the trial of Lindsay Clancy for one hour to allow her lawyer to file an appeal with a higher court. The jury has been deadlocked 11-1 with the majority apparently leaning towards finding the 36-year-old Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity. Clancy has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, saying she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children.

items.title: Pas political cooperation subject to Syura Ulama Council review
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas says all political cooperation it undertakes is carefully scrutinised and reviewed before being referred to its Syura Ulama Council for guidance. Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the party's decisions were guided by the council. That is why Pas has never lost out through its political cooperation," he said.

items.title: Pas won't sacrifice principles just to win, reach Putrajaya – Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas is attracting interest from various quarters, with several new parties keen to join forces and work with it, says its deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man. He said Pas welcomed any party that wanted to work with it but would not sacrifice its principles for electoral victory. Tuan Ibrahim was speaking at the Pas 75th anniversary grand ceramah here today, attended by party president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang.

items.title: Fadhlina urges parents, schools to follow official haze updates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has urged parents and school communities to monitor haze updates through official channels of the Sarawak State Education Department to ensure children's safety. In a Facebook post tonight, she stressed that the health and safety of students must be prioritised, with the department continuing to monitor conditions closely. Earlier, the department announced the temporary closure of 647 schools from Sept 7 to 11 due to unhealthy API readings.

items.title: Sarawak Forestry ramps up monitoring in fire-prone forests as heat, haze raise risks to wildlife
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 4 — Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC) is stepping up monitoring in high-risk forest areas amid the current hot, dry and hazy weather, which could heighten the risk of forest fires. SFC general manager Abang Arabi Abang Aimran said the situation warranted close attention as the prevailing conditions could place additional pressure on forest ecosystems and wildlife. “We conduct monitoring, particularly in peat forest areas and areas close to human activities.

items.title: Malaysian durians could clear China customs in three to four hours under proposed fast-track scheme
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — Malaysian fresh durians could potentially clear customs in China within three to four hours under a proposed fast-track mechanism being explored by Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB), China Henan Aviation Group Co Ltd (CHAG) and Tropika Makmur Manufacturing Sdn Bhd (TMM). According to MAHB in a statement, the proposed “inspect-on-arrival and release-upon-compliance” model under KUL-CGO Smart Durian Fast Track would enable the entire process, from aircraft arrival to document formalities and cargo collection, to take only three to four hours. “The Smart Durian Fast Track will explore improvements spanning handling and inspection, free zone access, customs coordination, permit and certification visibility,” it added.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia, Macau to strengthen strategic ties and unlock new business opportunities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia and Macau remain committed to strengthening bilateral relations and enhancing strategic cooperation across various fields, including trade and investment, finance, science and technology, education, and the convention and exhibition industry. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that this commitment also encompasses efforts to leverage the strategic positions of Macau and Hengqin, which are connected to the Greater Bay Area (GBA), for Malaysian companies to explore business opportunities. The visit marks Sam’s inaugural trip to Malaysia since assuming office as Macau’s Chief Executive in December 2024.

items.title: MACC drops orange garb requirement for suspects brought to court for remand
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has suspended the use of the orange garb for people under investigation who are brought to court for remand applications, with immediate effect. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the move is in response to recent developments and current recommendations on procedures for handling people under investigation, particularly when they are brought to court. “Individuals under investigation may wear their own clothes when brought to court, while lockup attire will only be required while they are being held in detention,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar says orange detention garb unnecessary for those cooperating with investigations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Individuals who fully cooperate with investigations should not have to wear orange detention garb when brought to court before they are formally charged, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. “I said yesterday that before prosecution, or before a person is brought to court and charged, there is no need to wear orange detention garb. On Tuesday, a former minister was brought to court wearing the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) orange detention garb for a remand application in connection with an investigation into a hotel lease involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Transboundary haze poses long-term threat to wildlife, disrupting habitats, food sources and reproduction
items.summary: Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) Environmental Governance expert Assoc Prof Haliza Abdul Rahman said among the significant impacts on fauna were chronic respiratory damage, decreased reproduction rates, dehydration and lack of food sources. “The haze does not only affect humans, but also animals and plants. Haliza said thick haze also reduced visibility for wildlife, resulting in a higher risk of these animals straying from their natural habitats into forest fringes or human settlements.

items.title: Sarawak to close 647 schools for five days from Sept 7 to 11 as haze persists
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 4 — A total of 647 schools in Sarawak will be closed for five days from September 7 to 11 due to persistent haze with no significant signs of improvement. Sarawak Education director Omar Mahli said the closure involved 563 primary and 84 secondary schools across several districts, reported Astro Awani. The affected schools are under the Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu, Kanowit, Julau and Maradong district education offices.

items.title: King consents to emergency declaration in Serian as haze reaches hazardous levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, has approved the declaration of an emergency throughout the Serian Division in Sarawak following worsening haze that has reached levels hazardous to public health and safety. The Prime Minister’s Office said the decision was made after taking into account the advice of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg and relevant agencies on air quality in the affected area. The declaration covers the entire Serian Division in Sarawak.

items.title: TMJ says no issue paying Singapore tax on land sale exceeding RM4b
items.summary: JOHOR BARU, Sept 4 — Johor Regent Tunku Ismail Sultan Ibrahim says he has no reservations about paying a hefty tax bill linked to the planned sale of his 16.6-hectare landholding in Singapore. The Star reported that Tunku Ismail, who is also the Johor Crown Prince, responded on X to reports of a potential land betterment charge exceeding US$1 billion (RM4.05 billion), saying he had no qualms about paying taxes and contributing to both countries. The planned land sale involves parcels on Holland Road that Tunku Ismail owns following a land-swap agreement with the Singapore government in June 2025.

items.title: Anwar tells Rural Development Ministry and MOF to find middle ground in funding row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today called on the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW) and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to resolve issues concerning allocations, including delayed payments to contractors, through discussions. On Thursday, Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said there were no restrictions on KKDW allocations for rural road projects, with the full allocation for the projects having already been channelled. The issue arose following a statement by Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi regarding problems faced by contractors following delays in payments for projects under his ministry.

items.title: Anwar endorses proposal for SC or BNM oversight of Tabung Haji investments
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today backed a proposal by Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to place its investment operations under the regulatory oversight of the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) or Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). He said the initiative by TH’s new management, led by its chairman Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain, was a positive step towards strengthening governance and accountability at the pilgrimage fund management institution. Yesterday, Abdul Rashid said TH was refining a new regulatory framework to place its investment operations under the statutory oversight of the SC.

items.title: Eight men charged with murder over fatal Taman Alam Megah brawl
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 4 — Eight men, including two alleged secret society members, were charged at the Magistrate’s Court here today with the murder of a man during a brawl involving a group of individuals in Taman Alam Megah last month. Puwaneswaran, 39; A. Rhubban, 37; K. Thivagar, 29; Shaik Hasanudin Ahlauwudin, 26; Sheikh Mauludin Ahlauwudin, 24; and R. Darvin Raj, 23, nodded after the charge was read out to them before Magistrate Cynthia Noor Haizean Sulaiman. The remaining accused were unrepresented.

items.title: Prosecution to appeal Rosmah ruling allowing additional evidence, says AG
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 4 — The prosecution will appeal the Court of Appeal’s decision allowing Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction and sentence for corruption involving the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project. “It merits an appeal to the Federal Court. On Tuesday, a three-man bench of the Court of Appeal comprising Justices Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing and K. Muniandy allowed Rosmah’s application to submit additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction and sentence.

items.title: Court rules DNAA not applicable in Maju Holdings director, wife’s CBT, money laundering case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — The Sessions Court here has rejected an application for a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) in the criminal breach of trust (CBT) and money laundering case involving Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd director Tan Sri Abu Sahid Mohamed and his wife. Abu Sahid claimed trial to 17 charges involving CBT and money laundering linked to the proposed MEX II Highway project on September 8 last year. He faces four CBT charges involving RM313 million and 13 money laundering charges involving RM139 million, allegedly committed between May 2016 and October 2019.

items.title: BN backs unity govt despite push for earlier GE16, says Zambry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Barisan Nasional remains committed to the unity government and the country’s political stability despite calls within the coalition for the 16th General Election (GE16) to be held earlier, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir. The Star reported that Zambry said BN’s support for the unity government remained firm, stressing that calls for an earlier election should not be interpreted as confidence that the coalition would automatically regain federal power. He said there was no intention among BN’s partners to undermine or bring down the unity government before the next general election.

items.title: Malaysian man jailed six years in Australia for keeping Indonesian woman as slave
items.summary: MELBOURNE, Sept 4 — A Malaysian man has been sentenced to six years in prison in Australia after being convicted of enslaving and assaulting an Indonesian woman. Free Malaysia Today, citing ABC News, reported that Melbourne County Court Judge Michael Cahill sentenced Chong Chee Kit, 47, after a jury found him guilty of forcing the woman into domestic servitude and subjecting her to repeated abuse. A jury in May found Chong guilty of keeping the woman, who was in her 60s, in slavery between February and October 2022.

items.title: Penang steps up action to curb sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 4 — The Penang state government has taken several measures to address sewage pollution from pig farms in Kampung Selamat, near Tasek Gelugor, including requiring all farms in the area to send their wastewater to a biogas plant in Ampang Jajar. State Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman Jason H’ng Mooi Lye said the move is part of the state government’s efforts to prevent livestock farm sewage from being discharged directly into drains or rivers in the area. “The matter was discussed at a meeting with the state Veterinary Services Department and the state assemblyman for the area in April, and the state government has required all pig farms in Kampung Selamat to send their sewage waste to the biogas plant in Ampang Jajar since May.

items.title: Anwar to discuss further action on Sarawak haze with Abang Jo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Further action, including the possibility of declaring a disaster emergency following an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeding 500 in Serian, will be discussed with the Sarawak government, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar said he had contacted Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg yesterday to discuss the matter. This morning, air quality in Serian, Sarawak, remained at a hazardous level, with the monitoring station at the local District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 518.

items.title: Azalina calls for red flags at Desaru beaches after three teens drown
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — Pengerang Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has called for coastal areas in Desaru, including Pantai Tanjung Lompat, to be equipped with red flags and warning signs to deter people from swimming in high-risk areas. She said she had proposed the measure to the local authorities (PBT), particularly for beaches with strong currents that are unsuitable for swimming. She said visitors might not be aware of the risks, particularly at campsites without clear signs prohibiting swimming.

items.title: Lorry driver remanded three days over crash that killed 12-year-old boy in Gurun
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Police have detained a 40-year-old lorry driver over a crash involving a motorcycle on Jalan Gurun-Jeniang yesterday that killed a 12-year-old boy. The victim, Muhammad Ilham Firdaus Mohamad Iruan, 12, died at the scene from severe injuries. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the suspect was detained to assist investigations into the crash, Harian Metro reported.

items.title: Retired military officer with ‘Datuk’ title charged over alleged caddie molestation in Ayer Keroh
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — A 68-year-old retired military officer holding the title “Datuk” was charged in the Ayer Keroh Magistrates’ Court here today with using criminal force with intent to outrage the modesty of a 20-year-old female caddie last month. The charge alleged that Yahya used criminal force against the victim with intent to outrage her modesty at the Tiara Melaka Golf & Country Club golf course in Jalan Gapam, Bukit Katil, in Ayer Keroh, Melaka, between 8.30am and 12.30pm on August 25. The court was also told that Yahya had a prostate-related health condition requiring treatment.

items.title: Perlis police arrest activist over incendiary TikTok on Sri Veera Maha Kaliamman Kovil temple
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 4 — A 55-year-old activist has been remanded for two days from today on suspicion of making an inciting post via social media related to the organisation of a gathering concerning the demolition of a Hindu temple here on Aug 22. Kangar district police chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop said the man, who works as a consultant, was arrested in Petaling Jaya, Selangor yesterday at 10 am. He said that earlier, the Perlis police received 14 reports regarding posts on the activist’s TikTok application between Aug 22 and 27.

items.title: Third missing teenager’s body recovered at Kota Tinggi beach
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 4 — The body of a third missing teenager has been recovered from the waters near Tanjung Siang, following a tragic incident at Tanjung Lompat in Bandar Penawar. The victim, 16-year-old Muhammad Adib Hafiy Kamal, was found floating by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 11.15am today, approximately five kilometres from the site of the initial incident. Kota Tinggi deputy police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed the discovery.

items.title: MAG says mass drug screenings for Malaysia Airlines crew near 100pc
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has completed drug screenings for nearly all Malaysia Airlines cabin crew following the arrest of a pilot in Jakarta, president and group chief executive officer Capt. Nasaruddin A. Bakar said today. On Aug 17, MAG announced that all operationally active Malaysia Airlines pilots had undergone drug tests and tested negative.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines resumes Busan flights starting December
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 4 — Malaysia Airlines will resume flights to Busan, South Korea's second-largest city, starting December this year as the national carrier expands its network and pushes to return to profitability. Malaysian Aviation Group chief executive officer Capt Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the Busan service is one of several new routes the airline group expects to launch, including expansion by its budget unit Firefly, which recently added China's Kunming to its destination network. MORE TO COME

items.title: Two dead in Jasin motorcycle crash after overtaking manoeuvre fails
items.summary: Jasin district police chief Supt Lee Robert said both victims, a 21-year-old college student and a 41-year-old lorry driver, died on the spot in the incident, which occurred at about 11.30 pm. He said initial investigations found that the student was travelling from Bemban towards Ayer Keroh, while the lorry driver was heading in the opposite direction, towards Bemban from Ayer Keroh. Lee said police were unable to obtain any CCTV or dashcam footage of the incident.
